body.x: Legal Justia Co., Ltd. (CEO Shin Sohyun) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will be held from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas. The company will exhibit in the K-Startup Pavilion, presenting its advanced legal document generation solution powered by AI technology.

Legal Justia is known for its expertise in natural language processing (NLP) and recognition technologies, and it has earned recognition in the tech industry for its distinctive offerings. The company aims to provide accessible legal services to users across various demographics, empowering those with limited legal knowledge or experience to navigate legal disputes effectively and affordably.

Legal Justia will unveil its AI-driven legal document generation solution at CES 2025. Built on over 170,000 conversational legal consultation records, this solution excels in natural language recognition and processing. It automates legal consultation and document drafting, helping users articulate their legal cases effectively.

The system recognizes conversational language to extract critical legal facts and drafts detailed legal complaints. Unlike competing services that rely on multiple-choice questions and answers, Legal Justia's solution enhances specificity and accuracy by understanding unique situations and crafting tailored complaints.

Developed on an in-house AI model, Legal Justia’s solution has demonstrated superior performance in BLEU score evaluations, a standard for assessing language model quality. The system ensures that user responses align with legal intents, iteratively refining questions until a legally robust complaint is generated. This approach, combined with extensive legal knowledge and data, delivers reliable results.

Legal Justia offers users a streamlined process for answering chatbot questions in everyday language to generate legal documents, including complaints. The company also provides services for users who opt for this, allowing them to submit documents directly to law enforcement.

In addition to document generation, the service includes stress-reduction features such as access to psychological counseling, tools for evidence collection, and community forums for sharing strategies. These features address user needs throughout the litigation lifecycle.

A Legal Justia representative stated, "We aim to help individuals protect their rights and respond effectively in legal disputes, even if they lack legal expertise. By engaging with a chatbot in plain language, users can generate legally valid documents and access comprehensive support throughout the litigation process."
The company plans to use CES 2025 to showcase its cutting-edge AI technology and service excellence, targeting partnerships and investment opportunities in the North American market.

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
